The data most likely supports A, PKA causing plcg, but this is a judgement call rather than something the data establishes.

- **What the data shows:** PKA and plcg are weakly negatively correlated (r ≈ −0.19), so "no relationship" (C) is hard to defend.
- **Why A over B:** I only checked correlations; I didn't run a causal-direction test. This looks like the well-known Sachs signalling dataset. As I recall it, PKA acts as a broad upstream regulator, negatively correlated with most of the other measured proteins. Direct PKA–plcg edges aren't in the reference network as I remember it, so that part rests on memory.

ANSWER: A
